statement: 14 The reason we require on-chain user simplicity for Theorem 13 is subtle. Suppose the mechanism is not on-chain user simple and the users adopt different strategies for different distributions. The mechanism can potentially infer the value distribution based on the bids submitted by the users. However, when the mechanism is on-chain user simple, there is truly no information regarding the distribution that can be inferred from the users’ behaviour. The users will always bid their values in equilibrium. We leave as an open problem whether the same impossibility can be proved purely via off-chain influence proofness, without having to rely on on-chain user simplicity.
context: Second, we also rule out plain-text mechanisms that are simple to participate for a sufficiently rich class of distributions. At a high level, suppose there exists a distribution T and a value profile ⃗v for which the miner is awarded a revenue larger than the block reward from building an empty block. For another distribution T̂ with a monopoly reserve much larger than all values in ⃗v , by condition B from Theorem 6, all users must receive no allocation when their value profile equals ⃗v . However, the miner can deviate from the equilibrium behaviour, submit the advice aTmi corresponding to T and trick the mechanism into believing that the users’ values are drawn from T . The miner will then receive a revenue larger than the block reward, contradicting on-chain miner simplicity. 14 The reason we require on-chain user simplicity for Theorem 13 is subtle. Suppose the mechanism is not on-chain user simple and the users adopt different strategies for different distributions. The mechanism can potentially infer the value distribution based on the bids submitted by the users. However, when the mechanism is on-chain user simple, there is truly no information regarding the distribution that can be inferred from the users’ behaviour. The users will always bid their values in equilibrium. We leave as an open problem whether the same impossibility can be proved purely via off-chain influence proofness, without having to rely on on-chain user simplicity. ▶ Theorem 14. Consider the class T of smooth regular distributions T with no point masses, i.e, there exists no value v̂ such that Prv∼T [v = v̂] > 0. Then, a simple-to-participate plain-text prior-independent mechanism for all T ∈ T must be the trivial mechanism that almost never allocates any user irrespective of the block capacity or the distribution T . We defer the proof to the full version.

context: ▶ Theorem 28. Let T be a smooth regular distribution. Then, the only simple-to-participate generalized position auction for a finite block when user values are drawn from T is the trivial auction that almost never allocates any user. We leave as an open question whether there exist simple-to-participate mechanisms for unbounded distributions for blocks with a finite capacity. In the full version, we also discuss the challenges of designing an inference procedure to learn the prior T while being resistant to censorship and fabricated bids and leave open the question of designing such a procedure.
